proof.text: For every $m\geq1$, multiplication by $t^m$ on $\mathcal O$ is the $m$-fold composite of the monomorphism $t$, hence injective. So $H^{-1}(Q_m)=\ker(t^m)=0$ and $H^0(Q_m)=\operatorname{coker}(t^m)=B_m$, and the map $\epsilon_m:Q_m\to B_m[0]$ (zero in degree $-1$, the quotient map in degree $0$) is a chain map inducing the identity of $B_m$ on $H^0$; thus $\epsilon_m$ is a quasi-isomorphism [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. The transition $Q_{m+1}\to Q_m$ ($t$ in degree $-1$, identity in degree $0$) is a chain map because $t^m\cdot(t x)=t^{m+1}x$, and $\epsilon_m\circ(Q_{m+1}\to Q_m)=(B_{m+1}\to B_m)\circ\epsilon_{m+1}$ since both are the quotient map $\mathcal O\to B_m$ in degree $0$; so the $\epsilon_m$ form a morphism of inverse systems [def-weil-inverse-system]. Likewise the degree-zero map $\mathcal O[0]\to Q_m$ is a chain map compatible with the transitions, and its composite with $\epsilon_m$ is the quotient map $\mathcal O\to B_m$. The Lean proof uses Mathlib mappingCone.quasiIso_descShortComplex on the image under the degree-zero single-complex functor of the short exact cokernel sequence; monicity of endoPow is proved by induction.

proof.text: Choose the stated K-flat representative $P$ of $K$. Tensor each $\epsilon_m$ of step 1 with $P$ and use the total tensor complexes of [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves]. The cone of $P\otimes Q_m\to P\otimes B_m[0]$ is the tensor of $P$ with the cone of $\epsilon_m$; it is acyclic by K-flatness, so the resulting map $a_m:V_m\to U_m$ is a quasi-isomorphism. The transition formulas in the statement commute with these tensor maps, hence the $a_m$ form the strict tower morphism $a$. In Lean, apply the independent-coefficient tensor-preservation lemma [lem-pur-kflat-tensor-quasiiso-independent] to the canonical augmentation. This isolates only the acyclic-cone tensor argument, not the tower or reconstruction conclusions.

proof.text: Because evaluation of strict towers is exact, the levelwise quasi-isomorphisms $a_m$ make $a$ a quasi-isomorphism in the derived category of $\operatorname{Tow}(\mathcal A)$, where $\mathcal A=\operatorname{Mod}(\mathcal O)$. The strict-tower homotopy-limit theorem [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-strict-tower-homotopy-limit] supplies the exact derived inverse-limit functor, so $R\lim(a):C_t(K)\to R\lim U_\bullet$ is an isomorphism and is compatible with the strict augmentations. The Lean map on complexes of towers preserves composition componentwise by reflexivity, so the augmentation equation follows from the two functors map_comp laws.

source.place: Tag 0941, lemma-derived-limit-is-ok, functoriality of strict tower derived limits.

proof.text: The given distinguished triangle for $K$ is a Roos triangle for the tower $(U_m)$ in $D(\mathcal A)$ [def-weil-derived-limit]. Take the canonical Roos triangle $C_t(K)\xrightarrow{p_V}\prod_m^DV_m\xrightarrow{1-s}\prod_m^DV_m\to C_t(K)[1]$ of the strict tower $V_\bullet$ supplied by [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-strict-tower-homotopy-limit]. Since $a$ is a strict tower morphism, $u=\prod_m a_m:\prod_m^DV_m\to\prod_m^DU_m$ satisfies $u\circ(1-s)=(1-s)\circ u$; each $a_m$ is an isomorphism in $D(\mathcal A)$ by step 2, so $u$ is an isomorphism and $u^{-1}$ also commutes with $1-s$. Apply (TR3) of [def-weil-triangulated-category] to the rotated triangles with the pair $(u^{-1},u^{-1})$ on the two product terms: it gives $\phi:K\to C_t(K)$ with $p_V\circ\phi=u^{-1}\circ c$ and compatible third maps, i.e. a morphism of Roos triangles $(\phi,u^{-1},u^{-1})$. By [lemma-weil-pbc-r-lim-levelwise-isomorphism], applied to the levelwise isomorphisms $a_m^{-1}$, $\phi$ is an isomorphism, so $(\phi,u^{-1},u^{-1})$ is an isomorphism of the two Roos triangles. The $m$-th component of $u\circ p_V\circ\phi=c$ reads $a_m\circ\mathrm{pr}_m\circ p_V\circ\phi=$ the quotient map $K\to U_m$, which is the projection equation of the statement. The natural evaluation isomorphism supplied by the strict-limit theorem transports its triangle to the actual Koszul levels using a product isomorphism. The generic private Roos comparison proves both triangle equations for the same isomorphism; projecting the first equation gives the prescribed components.

title: Koszul reconstruction of a derived-complete reduction tower
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site with a sheaf of commutative rings $\mathcal O$, put $\mathcal A=\operatorname{Mod}(\mathcal O)$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], and let $t$ be a global section such that multiplication by $t$ on $\mathcal O$ is injective. Write $B_m=\mathcal O/t^m\mathcal O$ for the quotient sheaf. Let $Q_m=[\mathcal O\xrightarrow{t^m}\mathcal O]$ in degrees $[-1,0]$, with transition $Q_{m+1}\to Q_m$ given by multiplication by $t$ in degree $-1$ and identity in degree $0$. Let $K\in D(\mathcal A)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] and choose a K-flat complex $P$ representing $K$ [def-pc-kflat-complex]. Form the strict towers $V_m=P\otimes_{\mathcal O}Q_m$ and $U_m=P\otimes_{\mathcal O}B_m$, using total tensor complexes [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves]. The quotient maps $Q_m\to B_m[0]$ induce a strict tower morphism $a:V_\bullet\to U_\bullet$. Put $C_t(K)=R\lim V_\bullet$, with $R\lim$ the total right derived inverse limit on strict towers [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-strict-tower-homotopy-limit], with levelwise exactness as in [lem-weil-tower-category-levelwise-abelian]. Then $a$ is a levelwise quasi-isomorphism, hence is an isomorphism in $D(\operatorname{Tow}(\mathcal A))$, and $R\lim(a):C_t(K)\xrightarrow{\sim}R\lim U_\bullet$ is an isomorphism compatible with the strict augmentations from $P$.

Suppose additionally that $K$ admits a distinguished Roos triangle [def-weil-derived-limit] $K\xrightarrow{c}\prod_m^D U_m\xrightarrow{1-s}\prod_m^D U_m\to K[1]$, where $c$ has components the quotient maps $K\to U_m$ and $s$ is the transition shift. Then there exists an isomorphism $\phi:K\xrightarrow{\sim}C_t(K)$ whose composite with each Koszul-tower projection, followed by $a_m$, is the quotient map $K\to U_m$. It extends to an isomorphism of the two Roos triangles after identifying their products by $a$.
